scope: Nine Wave32 bitwise operations in boolean_functions, including selected half and preservation of the other half. Per-bit AND/OR/XOR/NOT/XNOR truth tables are a direct specification-derived exact reference, independent of numeric rounding. Every truth-table input at each bit and selector is checked, with exhaustive half encodings and deterministic full words. Exact integer results are required even when the API semantics selector is loose.
diagnostics: Per-output assertion identifies operation, CPU, modifier and lane; no opaque golden digest is used.

scope: Six Wave32 add/sub/subrev/add3 operations. int64_t computes signed or unsigned widened sums/differences without overflow (three uint32_t inputs sum below 2^34); explicit clamp then uint32_t narrowing implements saturation or modulo 2^32. Independent literal boundaries check operand order, signed limits, borrow and ADD3 clamp behavior. This simple integer model is an exact oracle; fuzzy FP comparison is inapplicable.
diagnostics: Boundary/random tests trace operation, CPU, clamp and batch; literal cases separately expose saturation and operand-order regressions.

scope: The 20 scalar operations in scalar_integer_call, their immediate variants and additional sign-extension checks. Hardware digests cover result low/high words and SCC over 4096 boundary/random pairs, both incoming SCC values and both semantics. Immediate ADDK/MULK computed references use bounded int64_t arithmetic and explicit narrowing; literal ABS_DIFF cases preserve its wrap-before-absolute ordering. Aliasing checks are differential memory checks, not separate numerical oracles.
diagnostics: Each hardware failure identifies CPU, semantics, incoming SCC and one opcode/immediate row (4096 pairs). Literal boundaries and exhaustive immediate assertions complement those compact row digests; dense-domain checkpoints are not needed for these small rows.

scope: 84 RDNA4 Wave32 FP16/32/64 CMP/CMPX predicate entry points. Exact mask results are anchored by hardware captures across modifiers, masks and input-denormal policy. The independent integer-bit reference applies selectors, ABS then NEG, optional flush, NaN unordered handling and signed-zero equality; sign/magnitude order implements finite comparisons without host FP arithmetic. Every half encoding is checked with representative operand pairing, not all 2^32 half pairs. Optional exception-state behavior is reviewed separately.
diagnostics: Hardware digest identifies CPU, denormal policy, mask and predicate. Independent boundary/every-half tests report predicate/modifier/input batch. DPP capture and per-output routing checks complement each other.

scope: FP32 RCP/SQRT/RSQ/EXP/LOG exact implementations borrowed from rocjitsu, both architectures and wave widths. Dense domains use retained raw hardware digests; modifier/exponent/special-value domains have per-policy/per-modifier digests. Rocjitsu-generated cumulative checkpoints reproduce all five hardware totals. DPP comparisons to a non-DPP invocation check routing/alias behavior and do not independently prove the numeric model. Architecture-specific NaN and OMOD assertions remain literal anchors.
diagnostics: Dense captures now stop at the first failing 2^20-input interval. Modifier captures localize to operation, wave width, FP policy and modifier (8192 inputs).

scope: Bit scans count leading/trailing bits by an explicit loop; MBCNT counts selected bit positions below the physical destination lane and adds modulo 2^32. Literal all-zero/all-one sentinels and lane-number composition distinguish scan/count semantics. Wave64 DPP is independently hardware-anchored to physical destination lanes. Integer outputs require exact equality in either semantics.
diagnostics: Literal cases and per-output checks accompany the compact Wave64 DPP hardware digest. Pair/complement and population sweeps isolate individual bits; a failing digest need not be expanded into raw captures.

scope: Eight Wave32 extract/insert/mask/reverse/align/permute operations. The oracle reconstructs each destination bit from the source bit, explicit signed fill, reduced count or selector. All offset/width/source-bit combinations and all selector bytes are exercised. Literal zero-width, sign-extension and reversal anchors supplement the model; PERM selector behavior is hardware-digest anchored.
diagnostics: Computed checks identify individual output mismatches; literals identify boundary rules. PERM hardware hash is supplemented by EverySelectorAndSourceBit, so extra raw golden arrays are unnecessary.

scope: Seven Wave32 low/high 32-bit and signed/unsigned 24-bit products. Magnitudes multiply in uint64_t (maximum uint32_t product fits); signedness is restored with unsigned modulo arithmetic after any saturation. High-word extraction is explicit. Literal vectors cover signed minima, ignored upper bytes, high words and clamp. These are specification-derived integer references, not approximate numerical comparisons.
diagnostics: Boundary/random assertions trace opcode, CPU, clamp and batch; literal and full-product reconstruction tests distinguish sign, high-word and saturation errors.

scope: Fourteen Wave32 signed/unsigned min/max/min3/max3/median and mixed min-max orderings. scope: Eight Wave32 shift/add/Boolean/packed-average combinations. diagnostics: Per-output checks and independent literal witnesses separate stage-order and byte-overflow errors; no digest-only oracle.

scope: Four Wave32 signed/unsigned 16/24-bit multiply-add operations. Explicit half selection/sign extension and int64_t product plus 32-bit accumulator remain within int64_t range. scope: Twelve Wave32 single-half integer operations reuse the independently widened packed-half oracle only for the selected values. scope: Eight Wave32 half MAD/min3/max3/median signed/unsigned operations. scope: Twelve Wave32 packed integer operations. Each half is independently selected and computed in int64_t; saturation is applied only to the specified add/sub operations. All 32 selector/clamp combinations, half encodings and literal ignored-clamp/count-bit cases are checked.
diagnostics: Per-output checks and literal anchors provide direct diagnostics; no new golden data needed for these simple integer rules.

scope: Six Wave32 32/64-bit shifts. The computed reference visits each output bit, selects the shifted source or explicit sign/zero fill, and reduces the count modulo width. This avoids undefined oversized/signed host shifts. Every count and source bit/complement, ignored count bits, masks and register-half aliases are exercised.
diagnostics: Per-word assertions show opcode, CPU and count; both register halves and untouched words are checked. No opaque digest.

scope: Four signed/unsigned packed 4-bit/8-bit dot products in both wave sizes. Base-radix decoding and int64_t accumulation are exact; clamp applies after the entire dot, avoiding x86 pairwise saturation. Rocjitsu ffc144c564c Dot4ClampPolicyMatchesArchitecture vectors explicitly anchor the hardware/manual discrepancy: DOT4 does saturate. Every element pair/position and modifier combinations supplement boundary/random tests in both semantics.
diagnostics: Per-output and literal rocjitsu policy vectors identify saturation/order regressions; no digest-only dependency.

scope: Nine Boolean and two conditional-selection Wave64 operations reuse the independent bitwise and selector models. Both semantics, selected halves, ignored CLAMP, DPP routes/all row masks, full/irregular EXEC and aliased destinations are compared per lane. The separate Wave32 strict-exact case covers all eleven entry points; floating-looking input words remain raw bits.
diagnostics: Failures print operation/modifier/lane/route, with guard checks; no numerical approximation or opaque digest.

scope: Six shift and eight bitfield Wave64 operations use the independent per-bit models, with full/irregular masks, lane-distinct inputs, all DPP row masks, aliasing and both semantics. DPP is rejected for 64-bit operands rather than silently routed. Upper-wave and multi-register outputs are checked explicitly.
diagnostics: Per-lane/per-word checks and guards complement the Wave32 literal witnesses. Bitfield failures report opcode/batch/lane; shifts compare each output word directly.

scope: Signed/unsigned 16/32/64-bit CMP/CMPX predicates in both wave sizes. Explicit sign-bit ordering plus unsigned magnitude comparisons avoids signed-conversion ambiguity, with half selectors handled before comparison. Hardware masks anchor predicate/modifier/EXEC behavior; boundary/random, DPP and Wave64 cases check exact scalar mask results. Chained CMPX proves inactive lanes cannot reactivate.
diagnostics: Hardware digests are per predicate/width/control row, supplemented by per-mask expected results and a focused chained-CMPX invariant.

scope: Wave32 16/32-bit conditional selection. The reference selects the condition-chosen source, then copies bits while applying only sign ABS/NEG and half selection/preservation. There is no floating arithmetic; exact bit comparison remains appropriate in loose mode. Hardware capture, every modifier/condition bit, independent EXEC, aliases and DPP test the nontrivial selector behavior.
diagnostics: Per-output computed comparisons and condition-bit tests complement per-variant hardware digests; no need for a larger raw golden corpus.

scope: FP16/32/64 CLASS/CMPX masks classify raw sign/exponent/fraction/quiet-bit fields, including both NaN classes, signed zero, denormals and infinities. An explicit ten-class Boolean model and known-class witnesses are hardware anchored. All class masks, every half encoding in Wave64, selectors, DPP and raw-class invariance under guest FP policies are tested. Output masks are exact even in loose semantics.
diagnostics: Per-variant hardware digests have per-mask/class/encoding companion assertions, avoiding dependence on a single broad digest.

scope: READLANE/WRITELANE/READFIRSTLANE in both wave sizes and semantics. Lane-tagged literal words make index modulo wave width and first-active selection directly observable; every wrapped index and active-lane pair is exercised. The zero-EXEC first-lane behavior is explicitly anchored. Scalar outputs may alias source storage, while other lanes and guards must remain unchanged.
diagnostics: Direct expected word comparisons provide fine-grained failures; no digest or computed floating oracle.

scope: DS gather/scatter and force-inactive gather. A destination-centric reference searches potential active sources, performs explicit 32-bit byte-address addition/modulo group size, and resolves collisions by source order. Literal architecture tests distinguish RDNA3 32-lane groups from RDNA4 64-lane routing. Deterministic masks/offsets and exhaustive gather pairs exercise inactive-source and alias behavior; this is a simple routing oracle, not numerical reverse engineering.
diagnostics: Assertions identify architecture, direction, sample, alias and lane; focused address-overflow/collision and cross-half anchors provide additional localization.

scope: Both wave sizes, all 65536 offset encodings. Bit-by-bit bitmask/quad/rotate routing and the manual FFT order form an independent reference; hardware captures anchor extended modes and masked behavior. diagnostics: Every offset/lane has a direct assertion; hardware digests are supplemental per wave/mask. Further checkpoints would duplicate existing localization.

scope: PERMLANE16/PERMLANEX16 scalar and per-lane selectors in both wave sizes. scope: Thirty scalar Boolean/shift/shift-add operations. Hardware result-low/result-high/SCC digests cover 4096 input pairs and both incoming SCC values, in both semantics and every CPU selector. scope: Forty-six scalar integer/floating/bit predicates. Hardware SCC digests cover 4096 inputs per opcode under eight FP states and both semantics. scope: DPP8 FMA/FMAC routing, FI, modifiers, masks and aliases. The captured corpus uses small integers. The computed corpus uses multiples of 1/8 in [-4,4]; products are multiples of 1/64 with magnitude at most 16, sums at most 20, and OMOD is a power-of-two scale. All nonzero results are exactly representable in binary32; explicit zero-sign/clamp handling anchors zeros. This bounded arithmetic proof justifies exact bit comparisons without assuming general FMA equivalence. Hardware digest remains an independent routing anchor.

scope: DPP16 enumerates every accepted control encoding and covers FI/BOUND, row/bank enables, masks and aliases; invalid encodings are rejected. scope: Four signed/unsigned half extensions and saturating pair packs, both wave widths. The independent model subtracts 2^16 or 2^32 in int64_t for sign extension, clamps to integer limits and packs disjoint halves. Exact comparison is appropriate in loose semantics too. diagnostics: The retained hardware DPP digest now has per-output computed checks with opcode, CPU, EXEC, descriptor, selector and lane. Literal boundaries and exhaustive half sweeps supplement it.

scope: RDNA4 byte-to-FP32 and signed-nibble offsets in both widths. All selected integers and power-of-two output scales fit exactly in binary32; direct integer encoding and literal bit patterns justify exact comparisons. Tests cover unselected bits, modifiers, masks, aliases, guards and DPP. The additional Wave64 float-to-byte test uses a computed ties-even/saturation reference and checks optional-state rejection; it does not independently establish arbitrary FP conversion equivalence. Its hardware anchors reside in the separate byte-pack family.
diagnostics: Byte/nibble DPP hardware digest now compares every output with the bounded exact reference and identifies CPU, EXEC, opcode, descriptor, modifier and lane.

scope: Five byte/nibble conversions, both architectures and widths, loose and strict exact semantics. The bounded dyadic encoding proof applies unchanged. The local OMOD policy table cites RDNA3 ISA 7.2.3.1. Every selected input, all eight guest policies and output modifier combinations are checked with deterministic unselected-bit noise. DPP adds mixed EXEC, aliases and guards. Invalid modes preserve output. These exactly representable results need no fuzzy tolerance.
diagnostics: Every-input assertions identify architecture, width, opcode, policy, modifier, semantics, CPU, batch and lane. DPP uses whole-buffer comparison with configuration context, rather than an opaque digest.

scope: Signed-half-to-byte saturation and RDNA4 FP16 field packing in both widths. Saturation uses direct integer limits. FP packing selects halves, quiets NaNs and applies ABS then NEG without arithmetic. The 66 gfx1201 digests anchor every half encoding across modifiers, including NaN handling. Wave32 and strict-exact Wave64 now check the captured inputs individually against the field reference as well as retaining the hardware digest. DPP/mask/alias tests compose these operations with routing. Exact optional-state reporting remains explicitly unsupported; loose state preservation is tested. No general numerical rounding equivalence is inferred.
diagnostics: Encoding captures now identify variant, CPU and exact input index in both widths. DPP hardware digest has computed routing/alias companions; literal saturation cases distinguish clamp and preserved-half behavior.

scope: Four FP8/BF8 widening operations, both wave widths. Finite codes have at most four significant bits and exponent ranges entirely representable in binary32, so direct integer re-encoding is exact. Raw gfx1201 hardware digests cover every code without NaN canonicalization and anchor exceptional encodings including NaN sign. The capture test now checks the computed decoder per code alongside the retained hardware total. Every packed pair, byte/half selection, unselected-bit perturbation, masks, destination overlap and guards are checked. DPP is tested for single-result forms and explicitly rejected for two-result forms. Wave64 regroups the Wave32 numerical capture; it is not a native Wave64 hardware capture. Exact assertions are appropriate even in loose semantics for this lossless widening.
diagnostics: Raw capture failures identify opcode, CPU, width, output register and code. Independent literal boundaries and per-output selector/routing checks complement the NaN-canonicalized DPP digest.

scope: Four packed/stochastic FP32-to-FP8/BF8 operations in both widths. Stored gfx1201 outputs anchor special values, overflow saturation, sign modifiers, destination placement and stochastic seed alignment; strict exact calls use these goldens directly. Both capture tests now also validate the computed reference directly against those outputs, independently of GoC. The reference quantizes in output-spacing units using double arithmetic, explicit nearest-even rounding or truncated seed addition. Deterministic boundary/adjacent/random inputs, six seed patterns and alias/DPP corpora provide supplemental model checks; agreement there is not a proof of arbitrary-input hardware equivalence. Retain the goldens for the empirical seed/special-value rules. Exact encoded comparisons also test destination-byte preservation; no blanket fuzzy replacement is justified for these structural checks.
diagnostics: Captured tests report source, seed, column and CPU in both widths. Boundary checks report source and second operand; the DPP digest has computed per-output routing companions. Captured-domain equivalence is explicit, not inferred solely from agreement with GoC.

scope: Six normalized signed/unsigned integer conversions from FP32/FP16, both widths. These are loose/fallback implementations: strict exact is explicitly rejected. The independent model multiplies the integer significand by 32767 or 65535 (less than 2^40), then performs one ties-even integer shift, avoiding a host FP product rounding into a false midpoint. Captured outputs anchor saturation, NaNs, ties and ignored modifiers. Tests now validate that model directly against all stored capture columns, without using GoC as the oracle. Every half encoding, every integer rounding boundary and adjacent float, deterministic full words, modifiers, masks and aliases are covered. Exact comparison of resulting integer fields is intentional; fuzzy FP tolerance would not test their rounding or preserved destination halves. Captured agreement is not a universal bit-exact API claim.
diagnostics: Per-lane computed checks report operands and mode. Both literal hardware corpora now report source, column and CPU, including Wave64. DPP final digest has companion per-output routing tests.

scope: Three RDNA4 packed FP32-to-FP16-RTZ or signed/unsigned integer conversions, both widths, loose/fallback only. Integer outputs use explicit truncation and saturation. The FP16 reference binary-searches for the greatest finite half magnitude no larger than the input; sign restoration implements RTZ. Literal captures anchor NaN fields, infinity, saturation and ignored output modifiers, and now directly validate the computed reference as well as GoC. Every half boundary and neighboring FP32 word, exponent/sign boundaries, deterministic full words, flags, DPP, aliases and guards are tested. Exact encoded comparisons deliberately check the specified quantization and packing; this is stronger regression evidence for the current loose path, not an assertion of supported strict exact semantics.
diagnostics: Computed checks identify operation, flags, operands and lane. Hardware corpora identify source, column, CPU and saturation in both widths. NaN-canonicalized DPP hash is supplemented by raw literal captures and per-output reference checks.

scope: Nine packed/normalized conversion operations across RDNA3/RDNA4 and Wave32/64. This integration suite reuses the independently computed quantization references reviewed in the numerical family tests. It exercises all guest policies and modifiers, ordinary plus two representative DPP routes, mixed EXEC, three destination/source alias placements and guards across CPU paths. It does not claim native hardware captures for every architecture or policy. Strict exact is rejected, optional exact global-state reporting is rejected for applicable operations, and loose reporting leaves state unchanged. Numerical result checks are exact quantization/field checks, not arbitrary approximate arithmetic.
diagnostics: Whole-buffer assertions report architecture, width, opcode, policy, modifier, route, alias and CPU. Individual numerical failures can be localized using the companion family tests; no large digest is the sole oracle.
